_README: Edge Function deploy holds and order (CUL-1147). Merging to main deploys every function whose shipping code changed since its last recorded deploy (.github/workflows/edge-deploy.yml): it runs scripts/deploy-edge.sh, checks the result, and records it as a GitHub deployment in the `edge-functions` environment. This file holds only what a person decides. `holds`: functions that must not go live on merge yet (waiting on an app build, a clinical gate, a migration), each with the CUL issue that gates it, why, and the fingerprint of the code being held. Delete an entry in a PR to release it; that merge deploys it. A change to a held function's code fails guards/edgeFunctionDeploy.test.ts until its fingerprint is updated, so nothing joins a held queue unnoticed. `order`: functions that must deploy in a fixed sequence when several change at once. The per-function deployed/pending ledger this file carried before (CUL-135) is in git history. Runbook: docs/edge-deploy-runbook.md.
_order: ask's live photo reads route through analyze-vomit and analyze-stool (Ask A8), so those two go first.

analyze-stool.reason: CUL-552 PR 2 (CUL-1810) consent HOLD (client-first deploy ordering): this code reads the owner's ai_consent row before every Anthropic call and fails closed on a missing row. Today no account has a row, because the client that asks for one (the consent sheet, the first-open sheet, the backstop and the Settings toggle) is CUL-552 PR 3. Deploying this before that client build is live would turn off every photo read, every model-phrased Signal sentence, every Ask answer and every photo extraction for every account, with no way for an owner to say yes. Lift this hold (delete this entry) in the PR that ships PR 3's client, once that build is the live one; the merge that lifts it deploys the function. Holds on the same ref, lifted together: analyze-vomit, analyze-stool, ask, extract-food-from-photo, extract-medication-from-photo, generate-signal. The fingerprint also covers CUL-1835's "sent only if you tap" rule in _shared/aiConsent.ts (a photo logged before the owner's current yes is read only on owner_tap; PM ruling on CUL-1913), which the photo reads use and the other functions inline unused.
